concepts.preferred_label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and medical history of meningioma, along with the genetic findings of a SUFU gene mutation, are consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome).

The histopathological features of buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces, along with clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma, are characteristic of Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma.

concepts.preferred_label: SUFU-related Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
concepts.why: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, along with additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples, suggests a SUFU-related Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome.

concepts.preferred_label: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
concepts.why: The location of the ulcer on the glans penis and the presence of atypical lymphocytes with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement suggest a diagnosis of primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

The presence of a reactive T-cell infiltrate and atypical lymphocytes could be consistent with a diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, although the clonal IgH gene rearrangement suggests a B-cell origin.

The presence of asymptomatic green-yellow welts and swelling of the glans penis, followed by the development of a painful ulcer, could be consistent with a diagnosis of lymphomatoid papulosis, although the clonal IgH gene rearrangement suggests a more aggressive lymphoma.

The presence of atypical lymphocytes and a clonal IgH gene rearrangement could be consistent with a diagnosis of extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, although the location on the glans penis is unusual for this entity.

facts.raw_span: A white woman in her early 40s presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and scales, along with the phototest results showing UV-A sensitivity, are consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.

The patient's skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with germinal centers, along with the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, are consistent with Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and excoriations, along with the lack of response to topical corticosteroids, are consistent with Atopic Dermatitis.
The patient's phototest results showing UV-A sensitivity, along with the presence of erythematous papules and scales, are consistent with Photosensitive Eczematous Dermatitis.

The patient's skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with germinal centers, along with the presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, are consistent with Lymphomatoid Papulosis.

rationales.F03: Topical corticosteroids are often used to treat atopic dermatitis, but their ineffectiveness in this case does not strongly rule out the condition.
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and excoriations are common in atopic dermatitis and photosensitive eczematous dermatitis.
rationales.F05: Scales and fissures on the lower lip can be seen in atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F07: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a germinal center is suggestive of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and lymphomatoid papulosis.
rationales.F08: The immediate negative phototest reading makes chronic actinic dermatitis and photosensitive eczematous dermatitis less likely.
rationales.F09: The delayed erythema response to UV-A is consistent with chronic actinic dermatitis and photosensitive eczematous dermatitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including erythematous papules and excoriations, along with the delayed erythema response to UV-A irradiation, support the diagnosis of Chronic Actinic Dermatitis. While Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma is also a consideration due to the nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, the specific findings of erythema in response to UV-A and the clinical presentation lean more towards Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.

Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Confirmatory skin biopsy performed

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including progressive itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques, milia, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the histopathologic examination revealing dermoepidermal separation and milia in the superficial dermis, are consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the COL7A1 gene, as confirmed by whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing.

The patient's symptoms, including pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques, and the presence of milia and erosions, could also be consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita, an autoimmune disorder that can present with similar skin lesions.
